heading: EXT. KEYSTONE FLATS TELEGRAPH OFFICE - DAWN

units.text: EXT. KEYSTONE FLATS TELEGRAPH OFFICE - DAWN
White alkali dust runs to the horizon in every direction.
The telegraph office is a single plank room squatting on stilts above the salt, its shadow long and blue.
A wire hums overhead like something thinking.
SILAS CROWDER, sixty, sheriff, with a mustache gone the color of ash, leans on the porch rail with a tin cup.
MAUDE TALLCHIEF, thirties, the telegraph operator, stands at the window in a man's duster, one hand on the sounder key.
Maude, how long since the line went quiet?
units.name: SILAS

units.text: Since midnight, Silas. Whoever cut it did it clean.
units.name: MAUDE

units.text: Beneath the porch, EARLY BRANNIGAN, nineteen, deputy, and still wearing his Sunday hat, sits cross-legged on the ground sharpening a pencil with a pocketknife.
He glances up at the sheriff with the hopeful eyes of a dog.
Want me to ride out and find the break, Sheriff?
units.name: EARLY

units.text: Not alone, Early.
units.name: SILAS

units.text: A voice rolls in from beyond the last fence post, rich and unhurried, a preacher's voice carried on a cold wind.
Sheriff Crowder! I've come about the wire.
units.name: ABEL

units.text: Silas sets down his cup.
Maude draws a revolver from the folds of her coat.
Early stands so quickly his pencil snaps.
Abel Whitcomb. Last I heard you were burying folks in Dry Fork.
units.name: SILAS

units.text: Buried a few. Marry a few. This morning I'm doing neither.
units.name: ABEL

units.text: A silhouette appears at the edge of the flat: a man in black walking with great patience, a coil of copper wire over one shoulder.
That's my wire.
units.name: MAUDE

units.text: It was lying in the road, Miss Tallchief. I figured someone was missing it.
units.name: ABEL

units.text: Early lets out a laugh, brittle and unsure, and Maude glares at him.
Silas steps down off the porch into the dust.
Early. Put your hat straight.
units.name: SILAS

units.text: Yes, Sheriff.
units.name: EARLY

units.text: Now go inside and ask Maude to send a message.
units.name: SILAS

units.text: Silas, the line is dead.
units.name: MAUDE

units.text: Then we'll send it the old way.
units.name: SILAS

units.text: He raises his hand to the sky.
The wire above them sings once, a high clean note, and falls silent.
